 * @copyright

 * @test @b eigen_svd_cdouble_noavx512

 * This piece of code aims to stress test the FMA execution units of
 * the CPU, among others, by repetitively solving the singular value
 * decomposition problem on given input matrices, which involve a lot
 * of matrix multiplication operations underneath.
 *
 * The logic comes from the 3rd party library Eigen. The first thread
 * that gets to run computes a "golden value" of the results, those
 * being output matrices "U" and "V". Subsequent runs have results
 * contrasted to those golden values and, whenever they differ, an
 * error is flagged.
 *
 * This particular version of the Eigen SVD tests go for double
 * precision, complex numbers input matrices and the (divide and
 * conquer) bi-diagonalization SVD algorithm.
 *
 * @note This test requires at least 2 threads to run.
 * @endparblock
 */

#include "sandstone_eigen_common.h"

using namespace Eigen;

typedef Matrix < std::complex <double >, Dynamic, Dynamic > Mat;
typedef Eigen::BDCSVD < Mat > SVD;

#define M_DIM 300               // weird dim on purpose

using eigen_svd_cdouble_noavx512_test = EigenSVDTest<SVD, M_DIM>;
DECLARE_TEST(eigen_svd_cdouble_noavx512, "Eigen SVD (Singular Value Decomposition) solving payload, which issues a bunch of matrix multiplies underneath, now operating on std::complex<double>")

  .test_init = eigen_svd_cdouble_noavx512_test::init,
  .test_run = eigen_svd_cdouble_noavx512_test::run,
  .test_cleanup = eigen_svd_cdouble_noavx512_test::cleanup,
  .fracture_loop_count = 5,
  .quality_level = TEST_QUALITY_PROD,
END_DECLARE_TEST

2	 * @file
3	 *
4	 * @copyright
5	 * Copyright 2026 Intel Corporation.
6	 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
7	 *
8	 * @test @b eigen_svd_cdouble_sve
9	 * @parblock
10	 * This is the ARM64 SVE-backed counterpart of @ref eigen_svd_cdouble.
11	 *
12	 * It runs the same divide-and-conquer bi-diagonalization SVD
13	 * (Eigen::BDCSVD) on a complex double input matrix, but the Eigen code is
14	 * instantiated against the SVE packet backend by compiling this translation
15	 * unit with `-DEIGEN_ARM64_USE_SVE` and a `-march=...+sve` target, and the
16	 * Eigen namespace is renamed (`-DEigen=EigenSVE`) so it links cleanly
17	 * beside the NEON baseline build.
18	 *
19	 * The matrix dimension is chosen at init time from the RAM available per
20	 * worker (see size_matrix() below): the largest N whose peak RSS fits the
21	 * per-worker memory share, capped at the largest N that finishes the whole
22	 * test (golden BDCSVD in init + recomputation in run) inside a 10-minute
23	 * budget, and floored at 300. An explicit override is available via
24	 * `-O eigen_svd_cdouble_sve.mdim=N` (300..6000).
25	 *
26	 * Because SVE instructions are baked into the object, the test probes for
27	 * SVE availability at init time using plain C (no SVE instructions) and
28	 * reports a clean CpuNotSupported skip when the running CPU has no SVE
29	 * (e.g. Kunpeng 920). On SVE-capable hardware (e.g. Kunpeng 930) the test
30	 * runs and stresses the SVE FMA/vector units for SDC detection.
31	 *
32	 * @note This test requires at least 2 threads to run.
33	 * @endparblock
34	 */
35	
36	#include "sandstone_eigen_common.h"
37	
38	#if defined(__aarch64__)
39	
40	#include <sys/auxv.h>
41	#include <asm/hwcap.h>
42	#include <unistd.h>
43	#include <cmath>
44	
45	using namespace Eigen;        /* renamed to EigenSVE via -DEigen=EigenSVE */
46	typedef Matrix<std::complex<double>, Dynamic, Dynamic> Mat;
47	typedef Eigen::BDCSVD<Mat> SVD;
48	
49	/* Runtime dimension mode: the template allocates and compares against
50	 * d->dim, which size_matrix() derives from available memory. */
51	using eigen_svd_cdouble_sve_test = EigenSVDTest<SVD, Eigen::Dynamic>;
52	
53	/* Dimension bounds, all measured on cortex x3b (VL=128 pinned, same
54	 * compile flags as this TU, 2026-09-19 — see the plan file
55	 * docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-19-svd-cdouble-sve-mdim-5800.md):
56	 *
57	 *   MDIM_MIN  = 300: the NEON counterpart's parity point; the floor.
58	 *   MDIM_TIME = 4400: the largest N whose FULL test time fits a 10-minute
59	 *                     budget. The framework counts the golden BDCSVD in
60	 *                     test_init PLUS the recomputation in test_run — two
61	 *                     complete decompositions. Measured single-BDCSVD
62	 *                     times: 2400→40s, 3600→134s, 4400→243s, 4800→322s,
63	 *                     5600→511s, 5800→563s, 6000→622s (~N³ scaling);
64	 *                     4400×2 = 487 s total (19% margin; 4600×2 = 583 s
65	 *                     leaves only 3% for load variance, 5800×2 = 1124 s
66	 *                     measured over budget).
67	 *   MDIM_MAX  = 6000: knob ceiling (6000 alone already busts the budget;
68	 *                     it exists for opt-in experiments on faster hosts).
69	 *
70	 * Memory model: measured peak RSS is a stable ~9.7-10x the input matrix
71	 * volume (BDCSVD's real-typed m_naiveU/m_naiveV/m_computed plus U/V
72	 * copies and workspace — N=2400→0.86GB, 4400→2.82GB, 6000→5.22GB).
73	 * The sizing uses 12x (20% headroom) of 16*N² bytes per worker.
74	 */
75	#define MDIM_MIN 300
76	#define MDIM_TIME_CAP 4400
77	#define MDIM_MAX 6000
78	#define RSS_MATRIX_RATIO 12.0
79	
80	/*
81	 * Choose the matrix dimension:
82	 *   mdim knob (if set)  -> clamped to [MDIM_MIN, MDIM_MAX]
83	 *   else                -> min(memory-limited N, MDIM_TIME_CAP), floored
84	 *                          at MDIM_MIN; never below the floor even on
85	 *                          tiny-memory hosts (300 needs only ~0.2 GB).
86	 */
87	static int size_matrix(struct test *test, int *out_nthreads, double *out_gb_per_worker)
88	{
89	    long pages = sysconf(_SC_PHYS_PAGES);
